newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DUTCH RIVALS HAVE MIXED EUROPEAN RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DUTCH RIVALS HAVE MIXED EUROPEAN RESULTS.

text.p: Feyenoord and Ajax Amsterdam, who have top billing for Sunday's Dutch first division clash, had contrasting fortunes on the European stage this week.

The Rotterdam club, flying high in the Dutch league, look well set to progress to the quarter-finals of the UEFA Cup after keeping Tenerife at bay to secure a goalless away draw in the third round on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, Ajax, already eight points adrift of their Rotterdam rivals in the league, suffered a second home defeat, to unfancied French champions Auxerre, in Group A of the European Cup's Champions' League.
That result leaves Ajax, four times European champions, sweating on qualification for the last eight, needing to beat Grasshopper in Zurich on December 4.

Ajax, who midway through last season boasted a record run of 19 games unbeaten in the European Cup, have now lost three of their last four European home games -- to Panathinaikos, Grasshopper and Auxerre.

The Amsterdam club's proud record of winning the European Cup three times in a row from 1971 to 1973 still rankles with Feyenoord fans, who quickly point out that Feyenoord were the first Dutch club to win Europe's premier crown, in 1970.

While Ajax belong to the select band of clubs to have won all three European trophies, Feyenoord, past winners of the European and UEFA Cups, came close to joining the elite last season, falling at the semifinal stage of the Cup Winners' Cup.
